newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -FTSE to make a dash to 4,470 then drift.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -FTSE to make a dash to 4,470 then drift.

text.p: The FTSE 100 index will launch itself into record territory on Wednesday, inspired by the dramatic finish on Wall Street yesterday, chartists said.
A move up to around 4,470 by the FTSE is possible today before drifting takes place, they added.

This would be in contrast with its motion over the past few days until Tuesday when the FTSE had laboured to make much headway and market turnover had reflected this mood of caution. But buying interest should return following the Dow's 179 point gallop on Tuesday.
By 0810 GMT, the FTSE was indicated up 22.4 at 4,455.6.
New York's performance should ensure that City dealing screens turn blue today as leading UK shares extend their gains from yesterday to send the FTSE careering ahead, analysts said.

And the market should be more fluid today as investors become less reticent as they see share prices go higher. Shares in the finacial sector as well pharmaceuticals and oils will again play a leading role in the FTSE advance to 4,470, they added.

But a swift move to such heights will make the market a little unstable because it will take the FTSE outside an upward channel formed by parallel trendlines connecting the intra-day highs and lows since mid-April.

A move into record territory today will also be a test of character for the market as invstors wrestle with concerns about the direction of Wall Street and political worries about tomorrow's election.

Positive factors for the market are that its 25-day moving average -- currently at 4,312 -- is making an about turn and going higher, and that market turnover on Tuesday picked up to 920 million shares traded as the FTSE jumped up 43 points against a modest 673 million shares traded on Monday.
